per_question.question: If a Private Duty Nursing provider terminates services for a Medicaid beneficiary, what notification requirements must they follow?
per_question.agent_answer:
I found the directly relevant NC Medicaid source: Clinical Coverage Policy 3G-1, section 5.2.4.1, “Notification of Termination.” I also checked amendments for both 3G-1 and 42 CFR Part 438; both tool results identify the current authoritative documents with no listed amendments in the corpus. Next I’m going to read the full neighboring section on reductions/termination to make sure I capture any notice detail to the beneficiary versus NC Medicaid.Under NC Medicaid’s PDN policy, the provider’s required notification is primarily **to NC Medicaid**, not a separate provider-issued appeal notice to the beneficiary.

## If the PDN provider discharges the beneficiary
The provider must:

- **Submit the DMA-3513 (PDN Discharge Summary Form) to NC Medicaid within 5 business days.**  
  Citation: 3G-1 § 5.2.4.1, [3G-1 Private Duty Nursing for Beneficiaries Age 21 and Older](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

## If the provider ends PDN because another payer/source will cover nursing care
The provider must, **within 5 business days**:

- **Notify NC Medicaid**, and
- **Submit the DMA-3513**, and
- Include:
  - **the last date PDN services were provided and can be billed to Medicaid**, and
  - **the name of the other source of coverage**.  
  Citation: 3G-1 § 5.2.4.1, [3G-1 Private Duty Nursing for Beneficiaries Age 21 and Older](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

## If the attending physician discharges the beneficiary
The PDN provider must, **within 5 business days**, send NC Medicaid:

- **the attending physician’s order to terminate PDN services**, and
- **the DMA-3513 (PDN Discharge Summary Form)**.  
  Citation: 3G-1 § 5.2.4.1, [3G-1 Private Duty Nursing for Beneficiaries Age 21 and Older](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

## Appeal-rights notice
The policy distinguishes between a **provider/physician discharge** and an **NC Medicaid adverse action**:

- If the **provider and/or attending physician** discharges the beneficiary, that decision **“cannot be appealed to NC Medicaid.”**
- If **NC Medicaid** terminates PDN because eligibility, policy criteria, or medical necessity is not met, **NC Medicaid or its designee must provide written notice to the beneficiary/legal representative, including information about appeal rights.**  
  Citation: 3G-1 § 5.2.4.1, [3G-1 Private Duty Nursing for Beneficiaries Age 21 and Older](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

## Related point
If services stop because the beneficiary loses Medicaid eligibility, or **no PDN services are provided for 30 consecutive days** for any reason (including hospitalization), the **prior approval process must be started again**.  
Citation: 3G-1 § 5.2.4.1, [3G-1 Private Duty Nursing for Beneficiaries Age 21 and Older](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment)

## Bottom line
For a PDN provider-initiated termination, the policy requires the provider to **notify NC Medicaid and submit the required discharge paperwork within 5 business days**. The policy text I retrieved does **not** say the provider must itself issue a Medicaid adverse-action notice with appeal rights to the beneficiary; that written appeal-rights notice is required when **NC Medicaid** is the entity terminating PDN.

Amendment check: I checked amendments for [3G-1 Private Duty Nursing for Beneficiaries Age 21 and Older](https://medicaid.ncdhhs.gov/3g-1-private-duty-nursing-beneficiaries-age-21-and-older/download?attachment), and the tool returned that document as the authoritative current document in the corpus.

The agent correctly cites Clinical Coverage Policy 3G-1, Section 5.2.4.1 with specific links. No hallucinated facts are present - all claims align with the evidence sections. The answer goes beyond the reference answer by including the physician discharge scenario and the 30-day gap rule, which are accurate additions from the same policy section.
